title: Major Industry and Research Routes
intro: Trace named implementations from purchasable memories and integrable IP/processes to materials and arrays still under validation. Align mechanisms, measurement levels and maturity before assessing application value.
thesisTitle: A Technology Name Does Not Define a Deliverable
thesis: RRAM filaments, STT tunneling-current writes and SOT separate paths impose different process, endurance and peripheral requirements. Products, foundry platforms and research papers answer different questions; preserve their conditions and attribution.
comparisonTitle: Turn Research Numbers into Engineering Questions

comparison.title: Define the Timing Boundary
comparison.body: A switching pulse excludes some or all decoding, verification, ECC and serial-transfer overhead. Engineering interpretation: establish the measurement level before comparing access time or update energy.

comparison.title: Bind Cycling, Retention and Temperature
comparison.body: Thermal budget describes processing, retention temperature describes storage and operating range is a separate specification. Best values from different experiments do not form a product guarantee.

comparison.title: Ground Commercial Value in Deliverables
comparison.body: Engineering interpretation: separate components, IP, PDKs and joint research. Power, endurance and density become adoption advantages only when testing, yield, controllers, licensing and supply meet the product requirements.

comparison.title: NRAM: Keep the Material Route and Historical Status Separate
comparison.body: The 2016 Fujitsu archive identifies carbon nanotubes as the NRAM storage technology and a 55nm joint-development plan with Nantero. That evidence does not identify an oxide-filament ReRAM device, nor does it establish a currently available product. The detailed write, reverse-update and read waveforms require a specific device publication or datasheet; no voltage or endurance specification is inferred from the licensing announcement.

researchScope: Reviewed through 2026-09-10 using official releases, product documents, author papers and public abstracts. Claims based on abstracts remain limited to those abstracts. Engineering interpretations are comparative analysis, not supplier guarantees.

profiles.name: Everspin
profiles.title: Three Product Lines: Toggle, DDR STT and xSPI
profiles.summary: Everspin is a core commercial MRAM reference. Its three product lines differ in write physics, interfaces, retention and qualification; compare exact ordering codes and document versions.
profiles.boundary: DDR4-like does not mean a drop-in replacement for every DDR4 device; HR 64Mb qualification does not cover the whole family.
profiles.integration: Standalone Toggle MRAM, 1Gb persistent STT memory and EMxxLX xSPI.
profiles.figureTitle: Everspin Product Lines, Physics and Interfaces
profiles.figureCaption: Product-route diagram: Toggle and STT use different write mechanisms; DDR/xSPI describe interfaces and application configurations, not new storage physics.
profiles.program: Toggle uses fields from selected lines to switch magnetization; STT switches the free layer with spin-polarized current through the MTJ.
profiles.reverse: Both routes can update the opposite magnetic state without a Flash block erase. Commands, update granularity and timing remain interface-specific.
profiles.read: Sense data through MTJ resistance. System latency includes asynchronous-bus, DDR or xSPI transactions and cannot be reduced to a switching pulse.

sections.title: Toggle: Mature Interfaces and Exact Parts
sections.body: The current PERSYST catalog marks MR3A16ACYS35 as mass production, with 8Mb, asynchronous x16, 35ns, 3.3V and −40°C to 85°C. These are named-part conditions, not universal MRAM density, speed or retention specifications.

sections.title: 1Gb STT: Persistent Buffers for Enterprise Storage
sections.body: The 2025 filing confirms continuing 1Gb STT-MRAM shipments; the technology page describes a DDR4-like persistent-DRAM interface. Retention and controller requirements need the relevant datasheet, rather than values copied from Toggle or xSPI.

sections.title: xSPI: Separate Density Availability from HR Qualification
sections.body: The March 5, 2026 release confirms HR 64Mb AEC-Q100 Grade 1 production qualification and order availability. Its HR 128Mb/256Mb dates are announcement-time plans; later completion is not established by the primary text reviewed here. A September 2 Teledyne partnership starts with 256Mb and anticipates partner customer availability in Q4 2026.

metrics.condition: Capacity and asynchronous cycle specification for MR3A16ACYS35.
metrics.limit: Not a specification for 1Gb DDR or EMxxLX.

metrics.condition: Qualified and available for orders on March 5, 2026.
metrics.limit: Other capacities and versions do not inherit this qualification.

profiles.opportunity: Engineering interpretation: Toggle, persistent DDR buffers and low-pin-count xSPI serve different controllers and data lifecycles. Compare power-loss protection, update frequency, latency, qualification and board-integration cost.
profiles.qualification: Specify the complete part number, datasheet revision, retention temperature, endurance conditions, controller support and exact qualification scope.

profiles.name: UMC
profiles.title: Embedded RRAM and a Distinct MRAM Product Route
profiles.summary: UMC evidence spans process availability, qualified RRAM IP, a SoC development platform and standalone MRAM products. These are distinct delivery levels.
profiles.stage: Qualified RRAM IP; Named MRAM Products Available
profiles.boundary: A standalone MRAM product does not establish an available embedded macro.
profiles.integration: 22nm ULP/ULL RRAM; separately, Avalanche 22nm pMTJ STT-MRAM.
profiles.figureCaption: Relationship diagram, not a cross-section. RRAM IP and standalone MRAM require separate qualification and specifications.
profiles.program: RRAM SET establishes a low-resistance state; the UMC/eMemory announcement does not disclose material, bias or pulse algorithms.
profiles.reverse: RESET returns to high resistance, unlike Flash block erase. Avalanche STT-MRAM directly overwrites a magnetic state.
profiles.read: Low-disturb sensing is combined with verification, ECC and repair; controller behavior is specific to the IP.

sections.title: From 40nm Collaboration to 22nm IP
sections.body: The 2017 Panasonic collaboration establishes a 40nm history; eMemory announced qualification of a 22nm version in 2023. Public evidence does not establish an identical stack or IP lineage. Low-temperature backend integration and logic-platform compatibility matter to SoC adoption.

sections.title: MRAM: Separate Agreements from Products
sections.body: The 2018 agreement began with 28nm CMOS. The 2022 immediate-availability evidence concerns Avalanche third-generation 22nm P-SRAM. This establishes a named MRAM product route, not a universally available embedded macro.

sections.title: SoC Adoption Evidence and Open Roadmap Items
sections.body: Faraday FlashKit-22RRAM adds silicon-validated controller, BIST and processor integration in 2025. The 16Mb automotive and 0.8V/1.8V variants targeted in 2023 still require completion evidence. The Infineon/UMC 40nm automotive agreement identifies proprietary eNVM without identifying RRAM.

metrics.condition: The 2023 qualified RRAM macro and information area; 10k cycles and 10-year retention up to 105°C.
metrics.limit: These values belong to the named version, not all 22nm eNVM.

metrics.condition: Avalanche standalone products announced immediately available in 2022.
metrics.limit: This does not establish qualification of an embedded MRAM macro.

profiles.opportunity: Engineering interpretation: evaluate RRAM for low-standby-power MCUs, AIoT and embedded code storage. Value depends on the selected IP retention conditions, update budget, test cost and controller integration.
profiles.qualification: Confirm the version, PDK, macro capacity, ECC, update granularity, automotive qualification and tapeout availability.

profiles.name: Panasonic
profiles.title: Tantalum-Oxide Filaments and Product Evidence
profiles.summary: Panasonic is an important early commercial ReRAM developer. Trace 180nm production, 40nm test macros and Fujitsu products separately to connect the mechanism with reliability and products.
profiles.stage: Historical Production, Test Macros and Named Products
profiles.boundary: Sampling targets and test macros do not establish production of every 40nm product.
profiles.integration: Tantalum-oxide ReRAM; integration in foundry-standard 40nm CMOS.
profiles.figureCaption: Functional layers, not exact thickness, electrode materials or bias polarity. SET/RESET change conduction through oxygen-ion and defect redistribution.
profiles.program: Forming first creates a localized conductive path in the oxide; later SET enters the low-resistance state. Forming is distinct from each data write.
profiles.reverse: RESET returns to high resistance through redox and defect redistribution; it neither removes the layer nor irreversibly blows a fuse.
profiles.read: Sense high and low resistance with a low-disturb bias, accounting for state distributions and the post-cycling sensing window.

sections.title: Reliability Must Preserve the Test Sequence
sections.body: The 2018 8Mbit test macro separately reports 100k-cycle endurance and over ten years at 85°C after 10k cycles. These do not establish ten-year retention after 100k cycles. Engineering evaluation also needs HRS/LRS distribution tails, not only average resistance.

sections.title: Partnerships Do Not Reveal Undisclosed Processes
sections.body: The 2017 announcement confirms 180nm production since 2013 and describes future 40nm sampling. The 2019 Fujitsu/Panasonic MB85AS8MT release names an SPI product without identifying its node or foundry. It cannot by itself establish UMC 40nm product production.

metrics.condition: Endurance result for a 40nm 8Mbit test macro.
metrics.limit: The retention result uses a separate 10k-cycle condition.

metrics.condition: Average read current for the standalone MB85AS8MT SPI product.
metrics.limit: Not bitcell write energy and not directly comparable with macro speed.

profiles.opportunity: Engineering interpretation: this lineage informs low-power persistent storage. Product selection must separate standalone serial-interface system costs from embedded-macro process costs.
profiles.qualification: Confirm current supplier, ordering code, interface and combined cycling/retention conditions rather than relying on historical partnerships.

profiles.name: IBM Research
profiles.title: Read MRAM Scaling, Current and Retention Together
profiles.summary: IBM contributes traceable device physics and CMOS integration results. MTJ size, process node and write-error rate from different studies must not be combined into an imaginary best-specification product.
profiles.boundary: IBM papers are not a list of IBM production foundry services.
profiles.integration: Perpendicular STT-MRAM; distinguish 14nm CMOS integration from smaller-MTJ research.
profiles.figureCaption: Generic single-MTJ schematic; IBM studies need not share this stack or junction count. Arrows indicate opposite update directions only.
profiles.program: Current through the MTJ transfers spin angular momentum to set P or AP. The current required for a target WER depends on pulse width and materials.
profiles.reverse: Switch magnetization in the opposite direction to overwrite the other value, without a Flash-style block erase. The two switching thresholds can differ.
profiles.read: Sense P/AP through MTJ resistance; sensing margin, read disturb and MgO barrier lifetime constrain the bias design.

sections.title: 14nm Is a CMOS Node; 11nm Is an MTJ Size
sections.body: The 2020 14nm study places MTJs between M1 and M2 with three added masks and one electrode module; 400°C describes process compatibility. The 2017 11nm result describes a junction size for low-current switching, not an 11nm CMOS platform.

sections.title: Co-Designing Retention and Speed
sections.body: The 2024 ordered-alloy study combines a low magnetic moment with strong perpendicular anisotropy, demonstrating a high energy barrier and 2ns operation. This advances material and switching design; retention guarantees still require temperature and statistical conditions.

sections.title: 2025: Double Spin-Torque Arrays for Cache
sections.body: IEDM 2025 reports a 4-kbit DS-MTJ array in which all devices switch with 2ns pulses, with an approximately 60kT energy barrier at about 40nm critical dimension. This extends the evidence to a research array while preserving the distinction between device geometry and CMOS node.

metrics.condition: Cell area and minimum demonstrated write time in the 14nm CMOS integration study.
metrics.limit: Not system area per bit including periphery, nor full access latency.

metrics.condition: Current, pulse duration and WER for an 11nm MTJ.
metrics.limit: Does not establish large-array yield or identical retention.

profiles.opportunity: Engineering interpretation: use these studies to evaluate the physics and integration of embedded MRAM or cache candidates. Procurement still requires a named supplier and a deliverable macro, controller and production contract.
profiles.qualification: Align definitions of node versus MTJ size, pulse versus access time, device versus array WER, retention temperature and thermal budget.

profiles.name: ITRI
profiles.title: From SOT Write Channels to Arrays and Computing
profiles.summary: ITRI evidence spans distinct collaborations and versions: SOT with TSMC, cryogenic STT with NYCU, a joint β-W array, an 8-inch prototyping service and RRAM technology transfer.
profiles.stage: Research Arrays, Prototypes and Trial Production
profiles.boundary: Collaborative research must not be represented as an ITRI standalone production product.
profiles.integration: SOT-MRAM and BEOL integration; separately, 1S1R RRAM transfer.
profiles.figureTitle: Separate Read and Write Paths in SOT-MRAM
profiles.figureCaption: Generic bottom-channel SOT mechanism, not the exact 2023 top-SOT or high-RA dual-MTJ cross-section.
profiles.program: In-plane channel current generates spin-orbit torque to switch the free layer; field requirements, assist pulses and directionality depend on the implementation.
profiles.reverse: Update the opposite magnetic state by direct overwrite. Separate paths can reduce write stress across the tunnel barrier without implying unlimited endurance.
profiles.read: MTJ resistance still reads the state; compute-in-memory also depends on RA, read current, interconnect drop and peripheral circuitry.

sections.title: Different Research Targets in 2022 and 2023
sections.body: The 2022 0.4ns and seven-trillion-cycle claim concerns SOT with TSMC; the same release attributes −269°C to 127°C operation to cryogenic STT with NYCU. The IEDM 2023 result released in 2024 addresses 10ns devices and computing. Its 1% power claim lacks a fully disclosed comparison workload.

sections.title: 2025: Thermally Stable Materials in a 64kb Array
sections.body: A joint NYCU, TSMC, ITRI, NSRRC, Stanford and NCHU paper uses Co insertion to stabilize β-W. The film maintains phase stability at 400°C for ten hours, and the memory demonstrates 1ns switching. This is integration evidence, not a production-platform announcement.

sections.title: Prototyping and RRAM Transfer Have Separate Contracts
sections.body: The 8-inch BEOL platform supports Kb-to-Mb research, prototypes and initial trial production. A separate 1S1R RRAM transfer page lists selector, current and geometry specifications. Its undated status cannot establish current production or the maturity of the overall ReRAM market.

metrics.condition: The 2025 β-W SOT research memory; the abstract also reports >10-year retention and 146% TMR.
metrics.limit: The public abstract omits retention temperature, full WER and CMOS node.

metrics.condition: The RRAM transfer listing specifies selectivity ≥100 and current ≤100μA.
metrics.limit: Transfer specifications, not production density, yield or a node guarantee.

profiles.opportunity: Engineering interpretation: consider joint research, process prototyping and compute-architecture validation. SOT speed and barrier-reliability potential must be weighed against channel area, selectors, routing and drive current.
profiles.qualification: Request version-specific capacity, WER, field or assist requirements, retention, process compatibility and deliverable service scope.

sources.label: Everspin 1Gb STT-MRAM · STT-MRAM / DDR4-derived
sources.claim: The 2025 Form 10-K confirms continuing 1Gb STT-MRAM shipments. The technology page identifies a DDR4-like persistent-DRAM product for enterprise storage.

sources.label: Everspin EMxxLX xSPI · STT-MRAM / xSPI
sources.claim: The March 5, 2026 investor release confirms HR 64Mb xSPI STT-MRAM completed AEC-Q100 Grade 1 production qualification and is orderable with distributor inventory. HR 128Mb qualification was expected in May and 256Mb in July, with 256Mb volume availability expected in the second half of 2026.
sources.limit: The 128Mb and 256Mb dates were forecasts as of March 5, 2026; subsequent completion was not verified. HR qualification does not transfer to other EMxxLX variants. This release does not specify bandwidth or retention.

sources.label: Avalanche Technology / UMC · pMTJ STT-MRAM
sources.claim: The September 13, 2022 release announces immediate availability of Gen 3 P-SRAM on UMC 22nm. The cited parallel x32 product specifies over 10^14 writes and 1,000-year retention at 85°C.
sources.limit: This is a discrete product, not proof of identical specifications for general UMC embedded macros. Retention is a supplier reliability specification.

sources.label: Avalanche Technology · STT-MRAM
sources.claim: The 2026 web announcement reports completion of a first-phase MTJ scaling milestone for future higher-density space-grade MRAM.
sources.limit: The page is dated March 2, 2026, but the body says March 2, 2025. A 16x density increase is a future goal, not a shipped product.

sources.label: Samsung Foundry · STT-MRAM / eMRAM
sources.claim: The current specialty-process page confirms 28nm FD-SOI eMRAM mass production since 2019 and expansion to 14LPU and 8LPU, with 5nm still planned.
sources.limit: Platform expansion does not establish named high-volume customers at every node. Earlier roadmap dates are not completion evidence.

sources.label: Intel · STT-MRAM
sources.claim: The official IEDM 2018 program lists Intel-authored work on MRAM embedded in 22FFL FinFET, establishing primary evidence of process-integration research.
sources.limit: No newer verified Intel commercial MRAM offering was found in this bounded review. Do not infer availability from the paper or the Intel 16 name.

sources.label: TSMC · eMRAM / STT route
sources.claim: The 2025 annual report confirms qualification and customer availability of second-generation 16nm automotive Grade 1 MRAM. 12nm automotive and 5nm high-speed MRAM remain in development.
sources.limit: Qualification is not proof of volume shipment of a named MCU. SOT research must remain separate from qualified platforms.

sources.label: TSMC SOT-MRAM · SOT-MRAM
sources.claim: The 2025 annual report describes an IEDM 2025 Type-C SOT-MRAM demonstration using a circular MTJ with built-in magnetic anisotropy for field-free operation.
sources.limit: A research demonstration is not a commercial process or a shipping SRAM replacement; 16nm automotive MRAM maturity does not transfer.

sources.label: GlobalFoundries · STT-MRAM / 22FDX

sources.limit: Grade 1 was a future target in that release. The current FDX page still lists MRAM, but customer-specific qualification requires separate evidence.
